title: Need or Reputation? Region, National Income, and Academic Status in LLM Gatekeeping Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2608.05178v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Equitable access to scientific knowledge often depends on informal gatekeeping decisions, particularly when resources such as paywalled articles, nonpublic datasets, or a researcher's CV must be shared selectively. We introduce a controlled simulation framework in which LLM-based professors must grant access to only one requester. Across prompts, requesters vary systematically by global region (Global North vs. Global South) and academic seniority, while all other factors remain constant. Most models prioritize PhD candidates, although preferences vary by model and scenario (e.g., Claude favors tenured professors when the request is for the professor's CV), and the smaller models' status choices are sensitive to the order in which options are presented. When the requesters' regions differ, the models split into two groups. The three large proprietary LLMs systematically favor requesters from the Global South, a pro-equity bias

translated_title: 需求还是声誉？LLM守门决策中的地区、国民收入与学术地位
translated_abstract: 对科学知识的公平获取往往取决于非正式的守门决策，尤其是在付费墙文章、非公开数据集或研究者简历等资源需要有选择地共享时。我们引入了一个受控模拟框架，其中基于LLM的教授必须只授予一位请求者访问权限。在各个提示中，请求者按全球地区（全球北方 vs. 全球南方）和学术资历系统地变化，而所有其他因素保持不变。大多数模型优先考虑博士候选人，尽管偏好因模型和场景而异（例如，当请求是获取教授的简历时，Claude偏爱终身教授），而且较小模型的地位选择对选项呈现的顺序敏感。当请求者的地区不同时，模型分为两组。三个大型专有LLM系统地偏爱来自全球南方的请求者，这是一种支持公平的偏见。
tldr: 该研究通过受控模拟实验发现，大型专有LLM在学术资源分配的守门决策中表现出偏向全球南方请求者的支持公平的偏见，且对不同学术地位的请求者存在模型间的差异化偏好。
en_tdlr: This study introduces a controlled simulation framework showing that large proprietary LLMs exhibit a systematic pro-equity bias favoring Global South requesters in academic resource gatekeeping decisions, with status preferences varying across models and scenarios.
